answer: Edge-Diversity Routing Weight. Each agent gets transaction capacity proportional to the number of distinct network neighborhoods its traffic traverses, measured via routed paths held over a rolling window. A zephyr of activity confined to one cluster counts near zero. To pass, an attacker must sustain genuine links across many separate regions, which costs real per-identity bridging traffic and latency on each new node, and the quartz of that overhead scales linearly, so mass fake identities hit a hard ledge of diminishing returns.
